desc:
A highlight reel must show every moment of an event lasting T seconds, i.e. the whole time range [0, T], without gaps. You are given recorded clips; clip [s, e] shows every moment from second s to second e, inclusive. Clips may overlap, and you may cut a clip into pieces (so using a clip simply means its whole range is available).

Return the minimum number of clips whose combined ranges cover all of [0, T], or -1 if this is impossible. Two clips that merely touch, such as [0, 3] and [3, 5], leave no gap.

clips = [[0, 3], [2, 6], [5, 9], [1, 4], [8, 12]], T = 12  ->  4
clips = [[0, 2], [3, 5]], T = 5                         ->  -1

In the second example the moment 2.5 is not shown by any clip.
hints: Imagine you have already covered the timeline from 0 up to some moment reach. Which clips can you use next?
Only clips with s ≤ reach can extend the covered part without leaving a gap, and among those the one with the largest end is never worse than the others.

This is the jump-game idea. Sort by start. Repeat: among all clips starting at or before the current reach take the largest end, count one clip, and move the reach there. Stop when the reach is at least T, or return -1 if the reach cannot grow.
editorial: Let reach be the furthest moment such that [0, reach] is already covered (initially 0). Any clip that helps must start at or before reach; if none of them ends beyond reach the timeline cannot be completed. Among clips that start at or before reach, picking the one with the maximum end leaves us in a position at least as good as any other pick, because every later clip that is usable after another choice is also usable after this one. This is the usual exchange argument for interval covering.

Sort clips by start time and scan with an index. In each round, advance the index over all clips with s ≤ reach while recording the best end; if the best end does not exceed reach, return -1; otherwise count a clip and set reach to the best end. Stop as soon as reach ≥ T. Each clip is looked at once after sorting: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
solution:
def minClips(clips, T):
    ordered = sorted(clips)
    n = len(ordered)
    reach = 0
    count = 0
    i = 0
    while reach < T:
        best = reach
        while i < n and ordered[i][0] <= reach:
            if ordered[i][1] > best:
                best = ordered[i][1]
            i += 1
        if best == reach:
            return -1
        count += 1
        reach = best
    return count
